answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers cap every identity at one action per epoch. Each seat locks a 200 POA bond and signs actions with a secret key split into shares. One action per epoch exposes one share; a second action in the same epoch exposes a second, so anyone can rebuild the key and claim half the bond. A farm of 100 fakes must lock 20,000 POA, and each fake can still act only once, so splitting work like cutting timber across a canyon of puppets gains nothing; the fable of free extra votes ends at the bond.
